How to read this report. Each finding is one problem, written so someone who was not there can reproduce it.

Severity is how badly it hurts a user (Critical blocks a key journey or exposes data; Low is cosmetic). Priority is when to fix it (P1 now, P4 when convenient). Confirmed means the tester saw it at least twice; Unconfirmed means once, and it is labelled honestly.

The first screenshot of each finding shows the problem; the steps say exactly how to see it yourself. The coverage table lists what was and was not tested, so silence about a page never means it passed.

Findings

QA-CORE-01

Checkout total is wrong when 10 or more seats are booked

SeverityCriticalPriorityP1StatusConfirmedCategoryFunctional

Where http://localhost:4173/checkout · desktop 1280 · Chromium

What the user experiences

A customer booking 12 seats at $24 each is shown a total of $48.00 instead of $288.00, and the booking is saved with that total. The studio under-charges every group booking of 10 or more.

Steps to reproduce
  1. Log in with the demo account.
  2. Open http://localhost:4173/book and choose "Pottery wheel basics · $24.00".
  3. Date: 2026-12-05. Seats: 12. Click "Continue to checkout".
Expected

Total = 12 × $24.00 = $288.00.

Actual

Seats 12, price per seat $24.00, Total $48.00: the total matches 2 seats, the last digit of the quantity. 9 seats gives the right total ($216.00); 10 seats gives $0.00.

Evidence evidence/core-01-total-12-seats.png

QA-AUTH-01

Logging in puts the password in the address bar and browser history

SeverityHighPriorityP1StatusConfirmedCategorySecurity

Where http://localhost:4173/login · desktop 1280 · Chromium

What the user experiences

After a person logs in, their password is part of a URL. It is saved in browser history, can be seen by anyone who looks at the history or a shared screen, and is written into server and proxy logs.

Steps to reproduce
  1. Open http://localhost:4173/login.
  2. Enter the demo account (demo@acme.test / demo1234) and click "Log in".
  3. Look at the browser's network log or history for the request the form sent.
Expected

The login form is sent with POST; the password never appears in a URL.

Actual

The form has method="get". The browser requests GET /login?email=demo%40acme.test&password=demo1234 before being redirected to /dashboard.

Evidence evidence/auth-01-password-in-url.png, evidence/auth-01-network.txt

QA-CORE-02

Double-clicking "Book" creates two bookings

SeverityHighPriorityP1StatusConfirmedCategoryFunctional

Where http://localhost:4173/checkout · desktop 1280 · Chromium

What the user experiences

The Book button takes a moment to respond, so people click it twice. Each click books another seat: the customer ends up with two bookings (and two charges in a real shop) for one class.

Steps to reproduce
  1. Log in with the demo account.
  2. Open http://localhost:4173/checkout?class=drawing&date=2026-12-12&qty=1.
  3. Double-click "Book".
  4. Look at "Your bookings" on /dashboard.
Expected

One booking. The button is disabled after the first click, and the server ignores a repeated request.

Actual

Two bookings, AC-1041 and AC-1042, both "Life drawing · 2026-12-12 · 1 seat · $18.00".

Evidence evidence/core-02-double-booking.png

QA-AUTH-04

Login cookie can be read by page scripts and has no SameSite setting

SeverityMediumPriorityP2StatusConfirmedCategorySecurity

Where http://localhost:4173/login (Set-Cookie on the redirect) · desktop 1280 · Chromium

What the user experiences

Nothing visible today. If any script on the site is ever compromised (a bad dependency, an injected snippet), it can read the login cookie and take over the account.

Steps to reproduce
  1. Open the browser's network panel and log in with the demo account.
  2. Read the Set-Cookie header on the response to /login?... (the 302 redirect).
  3. In the console on /dashboard, run document.cookie.
Expected

Set-Cookie: session=<id>; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax (plus Secure once the site is served over HTTPS), and document.cookie does not show the session.

Actual

The header is Set-Cookie: session=<id>; Path=/: no HttpOnly, no SameSite, no Secure. document.cookie returns session=<id>. (Chromium treats a missing SameSite as Lax, so automated cookie checks that read the browser's cookie store report "Lax" and miss it; the raw header shows the attribute is not set.)

Evidence evidence/auth-04-session-cookie.png, evidence/auth-04-set-cookie.txt

QA-PUB-02

Pricing page scrolls sideways on a phone; pass prices are cut off

SeverityMediumPriorityP2StatusConfirmedCategoryUX

Where http://localhost:4173/pricing · mobile 390 · Chromium (mobile emulation)

What the user experiences

On a phone the pricing table is wider than the screen. The 5-class and 10-class pass prices sit off the right edge, and the whole page slides sideways when the visitor scrolls.

Steps to reproduce
  1. Open http://localhost:4173/pricing on a 390 px wide phone (or browser device mode at 390×844).
  2. Look at the pricing table, then swipe left.
Expected

The page fits the screen width; the table wraps, stacks or scrolls inside its own box.

Actual

The page is 864 px wide on a 390 px screen (document scrollWidth 864 vs clientWidth 390), so the page scrolls horizontally and the pass columns are not visible without it.

Evidence evidence/pub-02-pricing-mobile.png

QA-AUTH-05

Adding a slash to the bookings address shows a signed-in user as signed out

SeverityMediumPriorityP3StatusConfirmedCategoryFunctional

Where http://localhost:4173/dashboard/ · desktop 1280 · Chromium

What the user experiences

A signed-in person who opens /dashboard/ (from a bookmark, an email link or autocomplete) is told "You are signed out" and asked to log in again. Logging in again does not help on that address.

Steps to reproduce
  1. Log in with the demo account; /dashboard shows "Welcome back, Demo".
  2. In the same tab, open http://localhost:4173/dashboard/ (with the trailing slash).
  3. Open http://localhost:4173/dashboard again (without the slash).
Expected

/dashboard/ shows the same signed-in bookings page as /dashboard, or redirects to it.

Actual

/dashboard/ shows "You are signed out · Log in to see your bookings". The session is still valid: /dashboard without the slash shows "Welcome back, Demo" again. The trailing-slash address is routed to the signed-out view without reading the session.

Evidence evidence/auth-05-trailing-slash.png

QA-PUB-03

Cancellation and refund terms on the pricing page are too faint to read

SeverityMediumPriorityP3StatusConfirmedCategoryAccessibility

Where http://localhost:4173/pricing · desktop 1280 · Chromium

What the user experiences

The paragraph that says passes cannot be refunded and late cancellations are charged in full is printed in very light grey on a light background. Many people, especially on a phone in daylight, will not read it, and it is the text they most need before paying.

  2. Read the paragraph under the price table that starts "Passes are valid for 6 months".
Expected

Actual

The text colour is rgb(185, 188, 196) on the off-white page background; axe reports it under color-contrast (serious).

Evidence evidence/pub-03-fine-print.png, scan.json (axe color-contrast)

QA-PUB-05

Search button in the header has no name for screen readers

SeverityMediumPriorityP3StatusConfirmedCategoryAccessibility

Where every page, header · desktop 1280 · Chromium

What the user experiences

The magnifier button in the header is announced only as "button". A screen-reader or voice-control user cannot tell what it does or ask for it by name.

Steps to reproduce
  1. Open http://localhost:4173/.
  2. Tab to the magnifier icon to the left of "Log in" and listen to (or inspect) its accessible name.
Expected

The button has an accessible name, for example aria-label="Search classes".

Actual

The button contains only an SVG marked aria-hidden="true" and no text, aria-label or title; its accessible name is empty. axe reports button-name (critical).

Evidence evidence/pub-05-search-button.png, scan.json (axe button-name)

Severity and priority

Critical
Blocks a critical journey (sign up, log in, the core paid action, payment), loses or exposes data, or breaks security. No workaround.
High
A main feature is broken or gives wrong results for many users, or a workaround exists but most people will not find it.
Medium
A feature partly works, a workaround is easy, or only some users or devices are affected. Includes accessibility barriers on secondary flows.
Low
Cosmetic, wording, minor layout or hardening issues with little direct user impact.
Priority
P1 fix before release · P2 fix in the next release · P3 schedule it · P4 backlog. Priority is the owner's call; the tester proposes it.
